title: Index-aware iteration and a histogram with primitive consumers

blocks.text: `Consumer<Integer>` boxes every int it sees. The primitive specializations take the primitive directly: `IntConsumer` is `void accept(int)`, and `ObjIntConsumer<T>` is `void accept(T, int)`, handy when an element travels with its index.

items: `forEachIndexed(List<T> items, ObjIntConsumer<T> action)` calls `action` once per element, in order, with the element and its zero-based position.
`histogram(int[] values, int buckets)` returns an `int[buckets]` where `counts[v]` is how many times `v` occurs in `values`. Do the counting with an `IntConsumer` passed to `IntStream.forEach`.

blocks.text: Lists may repeat an element; values may fall outside `0 … buckets-1`.

cases.says: Each element reaches the ObjIntConsumer together with its zero-based index.
Each value adds one to its own bucket.
Equal elements at different positions each get their own position, not the first match's.
A value with no bucket (negative, or too large) is ignored instead of throwing.

concepts: IntConsumer and ObjIntConsumer take a primitive int, so no value is boxed.
